summary: Exited at +10.00pts after the position gave back 15.5pts from a fresh +25.50 peak in a single bar, with KMDR and PROPP exit signals both firing against the position for two consecutive frames. The signature that drove the exit was confluence of a large one-bar retracement off a new high plus two independent against-fires, rather than any single small giveback earlier in the trade (which I held through since PF-based backtests show cutting winners early is generally a loser). Next time I'd want to watch whether the leg-level giveback stat (which stayed low, ~8%, even as raw px cratered) is a lagging/noisy signal at fast timeframes, and weight KMDR's known lead-time more heavily than raw giveback percentage alone.
